title: A Wolf for the Crown
premise: Petra Brightwater has spent her life in Hollowmere, a valley where magic cannot follow, carving bones that whisper the voices of the dead. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley to seize her gift, she flees into a world where an ancient covenant between humans and the wolf-kindred is failing — and the long winter falling across both realms is its dying breath. Guided by the dead and hunted by the crown's inquisitor, Petra discovers she is the last heir of the bone-carvers who forged the covenant, and only she can rebind it at the Wolf Gate. She succeeds, but at the cost of her own voice among the living: she becomes the bridge between realms, half-heard, half-remembered, guarding the peace she bought.
about_author: Xanthe Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bestiaries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about liminal people and liminal places, and live somewhere with too many winters.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In Hollowmere, where magic cannot follow, Petra carves a dead woman's bone and hears her final words. The valley's elders warn her never to speak of the gift. Emotional beat: quiet belonging shadowed by secrecy — Petra loves her home but knows she does not fully fit inside it.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Crown riders cross the river — impossible, since magic should not find the valley. An inquisitor named Serel Vane carries a list of names, and Petra Brightwater is on it. Her mentor burns the carver records and shoves her toward the mountain pass. Emotional beat: terror and betrayal as sanctuary fails.

chapters.title: What the Dead Carried
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Fleeing through the pass, Petra finds a wolf skeleton carved with covenant-script older than any kingdom. Its ghost — a wolf-kin scout named Hallow — wakes and claims she is bound to him by blood-right. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; the first taste of a larger world.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Below the pass, villages burn under the hunt's writ. Petra sees gifted children caged for transport to the capital. Hallow urges her to keep running; she cannot. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into resolve — survival alone suddenly feels like complicity.

chapters.title: A Cage of Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra frees three children but is caught by Vane, who surprises her: he is himself quietly gifted, serving the crown to stay alive. He offers her a deal — come willingly, and the children go free. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; loyalty and truth begin pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Gilded Road
chapters.summary: POV Petra, with interludes from Vane's journal. On the road to the capital, Petra studies the court's politics through Vane's guarded hints. The queen regent hunts the gifted because the failing covenant's winter is being blamed on them. Emotional beat: dawning understanding that the hunt is scapegoat, not solution.

chapters.title: Thorns of the Capital
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the city of Corvane, Petra is displayed as a captured witch. Among the prisoners she meets Maren, a storm-speaker who knows fragments of covenant lore. Emotional beat: found family forming in captivity; hope kindling in a dark place.

chapters.title: The Queen Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The regent offers Petra freedom in exchange for using her gift to interrogate the dead — including murdered rivals. Refusal means the children die. Emotional beat: moral corner; Petra accepts and hates herself for it.

chapters.title: Voices in the Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Questioning royal corpses, Petra hears a dead king confess he broke the covenant deliberately, trading the wolf-kindred's protection for personal power. The winter is his legacy. Emotional beat: revelation — the crisis is human-made, and therefore fixable.

chapters.title: Hallow's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Hallow. Through the bond, Hallow shows Petra the wolf-kindred's side: their realm starving, their gate sealed, their young dying. Some kin want war on humans instead of renewal. Emotional beat: empathy across the divide; the stakes become mutual.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant Explained
chapters.summary: POV Petra with Maren. Piecing together crypt-voices and Maren's lore, they learn the covenant must be reforged at the Wolf Gate on midwinter night, by a bone-carver of the founding line — Petra's line. Emotional beat: destiny arriving unwanted; fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Ivory Court
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A jealous courtier exposes Petra's secret research. Vane is ordered to prove loyalty by executing her. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the one ally inside the system turns hunter again, or seems to.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Bone Garden
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Vane secretly unlocks her cell, revealing his own covenant-heir blood and his lifetime of cowardice. They flee with Maren and the children through the palace ossuary, guided by its angry dead. Emotional beat: redemption offered but not yet earned; trust fragile as ice.

chapters.title: Winter Closes
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The company races north as the long winter devours the land — rivers freezing solid, crops dying, refugees flooding roads. Vane's past sins surface when survivors recognize him. Emotional beat: exhaustion and doubt; the price of survival weighs on everyone.

chapters.title: The Kin Who Want War
chapters.summary: POV Hallow. Wolf-kindred radicals intercept the group, led by Hallow's estranged brother Skarn, who wants Petra's blood to seal the gate shut forever and let humanity freeze. Emotional beat: Hallow torn between brother and bond; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Trial by Tooth and Snow
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra wins a stalemate by invoking the old law: a carver may claim passage to the Gate. Skarn concedes but follows, hunting for a moment of weakness. Emotional beat: Petra's first true act of authority; she stops apologizing for existing.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Glacier
chapters.summary: POV Petra. They reach the Wolf Gate beneath the glacier — a vast door of interlocking bone and stone, half-dead. Petra learns the reforge requires a life freely given from each side. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the price comes into focus.

chapters.title: Skarn's Hour
chapters.summary: POV Hallow. Skarn attacks at moonrise; Vane dies holding the pass so Petra can work, redeeming a lifetime of compromise. Hallow defeats but spares Skarn, breaking the cycle. Emotional beat: grief and grace — the cost is paid in full view.

chapters.title: Midwinter Night
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At the gate's heart, Petra offers herself as the human half of the bargain; Hallow matches her with his own life-thread. Instead of death, the covenant remakes them both as its living hinge. Emotional beat: climax — surrender becoming transcendence.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Winter breaks. The regent, exposed by the dead king's testimony that Petra smuggled out, faces a reckoning; the hunt dissolves. Skarn kneels to the new covenant. Emotional beat: relief and mourning braided together — victory that costs what it costs.

chapters.title: Half-Heard, Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra returns to Hollowmere, now able to leave and return at will but no longer wholly of the living world — people forget her face unless she speaks. Maren and the children build a school for the gifted nearby. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming; identity remade on her own terms.

chapters.title: A Wolf for the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Petra, epilogue. Years later, Petra stands at the Wolf Gate each midwinter as its keeper, Hallow beside her, the covenant strong. A new generation of carvers arrives to learn. Emotional beat: resolution — the price of survival was everything she was, and she would pay it again.
